meaning: noodles; (wheat) flour

senses.en: noodles: 一碗面 'a bowl of noodles'
wheat flour (the full word is 面粉), the stuff 包子 and 饺子 are made from

examples.en: Noodles or rice for lunch?
examples.analysis: 面 is the food here: noodles, as opposed to 米饭 'rice'. A 还是 B? asks the listener to pick one of two options, and spoken Chinese often repeats the verb before each (吃面还是吃米饭). 中午 at the front sets the time.

examples.en: Two bowls of noodles, please, and one without meat.
examples.analysis: Ordering at a noodle shop: 要 + number + 碗 + 面. 碗 'bowl' is the measure word, so 两碗面 is 'two bowls of noodles'. In the second half 面 is understood: 一碗不放肉 'one (bowl) with no meat put in'.

examples.zh: 家里还有面吗？我想做包子。
examples.en: Is there any flour left at home? I want to make steamed buns.
examples.analysis: Here 面 is flour, the raw material for 包子; the second sentence is what tells you it is not noodles. 还有…吗? 'is there still any…?' asks whether some is left.

related.en: cooked rice, the other everyday staple
dumplings, wrapped in dough made from 面

hook: In simplified writing, 面 'face' and 麵 'flour, noodles' (written with 麥 'wheat') became one character, so context tells you which is meant.

meaning: at one's side; around one (people); on one, within reach (things)

senses.en: at someone's side, close by: 在你身边
the people in your life: 身边的朋友
on you, with you (phone, money): 手机不在身边

examples.en: Don't be afraid. I'm right here beside you.
examples.analysis: 身边 'at your side' is a place word, so it follows 在: 在 + 你 + 身边 'by your side'. The person comes first, then 身边; 的 is left out here, though 在你的身边 is also common. 就 stresses 'right here, close by'.

examples.zh: 你身边有会说中文的朋友吗？
examples.en: Do you have any friends around you who speak Chinese?
examples.analysis: 身边 here means the people in your daily life, not literally beside you. 你身边有… 'around you there is…' is a 有 sentence with a place word as the topic. 会说中文的 'who can speak Chinese' describes 朋友.

examples.zh: 刚才手机不在身边，没看到。
examples.en: I didn't have my phone on me just now, so I didn't see it.
examples.analysis: With things, 在身边 means 'on you, within reach'. 不在身边 'not with me' explains why 没看到 'didn't see (the message)'. 'I' and 'it' are left out because both are obvious.

related.en: beside, next to: physical position only, for people or things (我旁边, 银行旁边); 身边 needs a person as the reference point (你身边, 我身边)
on one's body; on one (money, keys)

meaning: all; the whole lot (every part of it)

senses.en: all of it, the whole: 这不是全部 'this isn't all of it'
before a verb or 是, sums up the group just mentioned: 这些菜全部是我做的 'all of these were made by me'

examples.en: I made all of these dishes myself.
examples.analysis: 全部 comes after the subject 这些菜 and before the verb, and sums them up: 'all of them'. 是我做的 is the 是…的 pattern, which stresses who did it: it was me who cooked them.

examples.zh: 这不是全部，还有一些在车上。
examples.en: This isn't all of it. There's some more in the car.
examples.analysis: Here 全部 is a noun, the object of 是: 这不是全部 'this is not the whole lot'. 还有一些 'there is still some more', and 在车上 'in the car' says where the rest is.

examples.en: You gave him all your money?
examples.analysis: 你的钱 'your money' is the topic, put first; 全部 before 给 says none of it was kept back. There is no 吗: the rising intonation makes it a question, and it sounds surprised.

related.en: all (before a noun: 所有的人 'everyone')
all, both (adverb, before the verb phrase: 都是, 都不去)

meaning: group, team; to form (a group or team)

senses.en: group, team at work or in class: 我们组 'our team'
to put together, form: 组个队 'form a team'

examples.en: How many people are on your team?
examples.analysis: 组 is a noun: a work or class group. 你们组 'your team' needs no 的, as with 我们班 or 我们家. In casual speech the verb 有 can drop out, leaving just 几个人? 'how many people?'.

examples.zh: 我们组今天下午不开会了。
examples.en: Our team isn't meeting this afternoon after all.
examples.analysis: 我们组 'our team' is the subject. In 不开会了, the 了 at the end marks a change of plan, so it means 'the meeting is off', not just 'we don't hold meetings'.

examples.zh: 周末我们组个队去打球吧！
examples.en: Let's get a team together this weekend and go play ball!
examples.analysis: Here 组 is a verb: to put together, form. 组个队 is short for 组一个队 'form a team'; spoken Chinese often drops 一 before 个. 去打球 says what the team is for, and 吧 makes it a suggestion.

meaning: to hand in; to pay (a bill, a fee); to make (friends)

senses.en: to hand in, hand over: 交作业 'hand in homework'
to pay a bill or fee: 交钱
to make friends: 交朋友

examples.en: The homework is due tomorrow. Don't forget.
examples.analysis: 交 is 'to hand in'. 作业 'homework' is the topic, placed first, and 明天交 'hand in tomorrow' comments on it, so no subject is needed. 别忘了 'don't forget' is a common tag after a reminder.

examples.en: Excuse me, where do I pay?
examples.analysis: 交钱 'to pay (a bill or fee)' is what you hear at counters in hospitals, schools and offices. 在哪儿 goes before the verb: 'where do (I) pay?'. 请问 opens a polite question to a stranger.

examples.zh: 你在这儿交了很多朋友吧？
examples.en: You must have made lots of friends here, right?
examples.analysis: 交 goes with 朋友 here: 交朋友 'make friends'. 了 and 很多 sit between the verb and its object: 交了很多朋友. 吧 at the end means you expect a yes and want it confirmed.

related.en: to deliver; to give as a gift

meaning: eye; (measure word) a look, a glance: 看一眼

senses.en: eye (in short spoken phrases; the full word is 眼睛)
a look, a glance: 看一眼 'take a quick look'

examples.zh: 你帮我看一眼，这个对不对？
examples.en: Could you take a quick look for me? Is this right?
examples.analysis: 眼 is a measure word here: 看一眼 'look one glance', a quick look. 帮我 + verb asks for help. 对不对 'right or not' turns the second half into a question without 吗.

examples.en: I just had a look. I didn't buy anything.
examples.analysis: 看了一眼 'took one look': 眼 counts the look, like 'a glance'. 就 here means 'only, just'. 没买 'didn't buy' uses 没 because it denies a past action.

examples.en: He cried so much that his eyes went red.
examples.analysis: Here 眼 is the noun 'eyes'. In short spoken phrases like this one, 眼 can stand for 眼睛. 哭得… 'cried until…' gives the result; 都…了 stresses how far it went: even his eyes have turned red.

hook: The left part, 目, is a drawing of an eye; 目 also sits at the bottom of 看 'to look'.

meaning: cat

senses.en: cat

examples.en: Do you have a cat at home?
examples.analysis: 猫 is the object of 有: 你家有猫吗? 'does your home have a cat?'. This is a common way to ask about pets. No measure word is needed because nothing is being counted.

examples.en: I'm scared of cats. Don't let it come over here.
examples.analysis: 怕猫 'be afraid of cats': 猫 with no number means cats in general. In the second half, 它 'it' points to the cat in front of them. 别让… 'don't let…' makes it a request.

examples.en: This cat is so cute!
examples.analysis: 这 + 只 + 猫: 只 is the measure word for cats and many other animals (though dogs also take 条 and cows take 头). 太…了 here is praise, 'so…!', not a complaint that it is 'too' cute.

meaning: everywhere; all over (the place)

senses.en: everywhere, all over: 到处都是人 'people everywhere'
(doing something) all over the place: 到处找 'look everywhere'

examples.zh: 我到处找手机，都没找到。
examples.en: I looked everywhere for my phone, but I didn't find it.
examples.analysis: 到处 is an adverb, so it goes before the verb: 到处找 'look everywhere'. 都 picks up 'everywhere' again: in all those places, 没找到 'didn't find it'.

examples.zh: 过年的时候，到处都是人。
examples.en: At Chinese New Year, there are people everywhere.
examples.analysis: 到处都是 + noun 'there's … everywhere' is a very common pattern. 都 often follows 到处 before 是 or 有 (到处都是, 到处都有), because 到处 covers many places at once; with action verbs it is not needed (到处找, 到处跑). 过年的时候 'at New Year' sets the time.

examples.en: Don't go running around. Wait for me here.
examples.analysis: 别 + 到处跑 'don't run all over the place' is what you might say to a child. The second half gives the opposite: stay 在这儿 'here' and 等我 'wait for me'.

related.en: everywhere, anywhere: 哪儿都有 'it's everywhere'

meaning: card (bank card, membership card, transit card, SIM)

senses.en: card: bank card, membership card, transit card
SIM card (手机卡)

examples.en: Can I pay by card here?
examples.analysis: When you are paying, 卡 'card' on its own usually means a bank card. 用卡 'use a card' is one natural way to ask to pay by card (刷卡 'swipe a card' is also very common). 可以…吗? asks whether something is allowed.

examples.en: I didn't bring my card. I'll just pay with my phone.
examples.analysis: 我的卡 'my card' is the topic, put first, and 没带 'didn't bring' comments on it. 用手机吧 'use the phone, then' is a quick decision made on the spot.

examples.zh: 办个卡吧，下次来便宜一些。
examples.en: Why don't you get a membership card? It'll be cheaper next time you come.
examples.analysis: 办卡 is 'to get a card issued', at a shop, gym or bank. 办个卡 drops 一 before 个. 吧 makes it a suggestion, and 下次来便宜一些 'cheaper next time you come' gives the reason.

meaning: news (on TV, online, in the paper)

senses.en: news, news reports: 看新闻 'watch or read the news'

examples.en: Is this news story true?
examples.analysis: 条 is the measure word for one news item, so 这条新闻 is 'this piece of news'. 是真的吗? 'is it true?' is a natural way to question something you have read or heard.

examples.zh: 我早上一般在手机上看新闻。
examples.en: In the morning I usually read the news on my phone.
examples.analysis: 看新闻 covers both watching the news on TV and reading it, since 看 is 'to look at'. 一般 'usually' and 在手机上 'on my phone' go before the verb, the normal place for frequency and place words.

examples.en: I've been busy lately and haven't had time to follow the news.
examples.analysis: 没时间 + verb 'no time to do something': 没时间看新闻 'no time to watch or read the news'. The subject 我 is dropped because in casual speech it is clear who is busy.

meaning: really, truly; just (can't), honestly

senses.en: really, truly: makes a feeling or apology stronger (实在对不起)
just, honestly: something is beyond what you can manage (实在太累了)

examples.en: I'm really sorry I'm late.
examples.analysis: 实在 makes the apology stronger: 'truly sorry'. It sits right before 对不起. In 来晚了 'came late', 晚 tells how the coming went, and 了 marks it as having happened.

examples.en: I'm just too tired. I'm going to bed first.
examples.analysis: 实在 + 太累了 says the tiredness is more than you can push through, which is why you stop. 先睡了 'going to sleep first' tells the others you are turning in before them.

examples.en: I really don't want to go.
examples.analysis: 实在 comes before the negative 不想 and stresses it: 'I truly don't want to'. It is stronger than plain 我不想去 and often sounds like a reluctant, honest admission.

collocations.en: if it really doesn't work out; if all else fails

meaning: pen, pencil (any writing tool); measure word for a sum of money

senses.en: pen, pencil, any writing tool
for a sum of money: 一笔钱 'a sum of money'

examples.en: Have you got a pen? Can I borrow it for a sec?
examples.analysis: 笔 covers pens and pencils; in this short question the subject 你 is dropped. 借我用用 'lend me (it) to use a bit': doubling the verb, 用用, makes the request light and brief.

examples.en: I forgot to bring a pen.
examples.analysis: 笔 is the object of 带 'bring': 带笔 'bring a pen'. 忘了 + verb means 'forgot to do something': the whole action 带笔 is what was forgotten.

examples.zh: 这笔钱你先拿着，以后再还。
examples.en: Take this money for now. You can pay it back later.
examples.analysis: 笔 is a measure word here, used for a sum of money: 这笔钱 'this money', put first as the topic. 拿着 'hold on to it'. 还 is read huán here, 'pay back', not hái.

hook: Simplified 笔 is ⺮ 'bamboo' on top of 毛 'hair', a handy picture of a brush (hair on a bamboo handle). The older form 筆 is built differently, with 聿 'a hand holding a brush' under 竹.

meaning: behavior, conduct (what someone does, often being judged)

senses.en: behavior, conduct, an act; a little formal, often used when judging what someone did

examples.zh: 他不排队，这是什么行为？
examples.en: He's not waiting in line. What kind of behavior is that?
examples.analysis: 什么行为? 'what kind of behavior?' is not a real question here; it is a complaint about someone's conduct. 行为 tends to be used when an act is being judged, as in this sentence.

examples.zh: 他的行为让大家很不高兴。
examples.en: His behavior made everyone really unhappy.
examples.analysis: 行为 'behavior' is the subject. 让 + person + feeling: 让大家很不高兴 'made everyone very unhappy'. 行为 itself is neutral and a bit formal; it is the unhappy reaction that shows his behavior was bad.

examples.zh: 别只听他说什么，要看他的行为。
examples.en: Don't just listen to what he says. Look at what he does.
examples.analysis: 行为 'conduct, actions' is set against 说什么 'what he says'. 别只… 'don't only…' and 要… 'you should…' give the advice in two steps.

meaning: side; edge; (by) the side of

senses.en: edge, side: 桌子边上 'at the edge of the table'
after a thing or place: beside it, by it: 门边 'by the door'

examples.zh: 杯子别放在桌子边上，会掉的。
examples.en: Don't put the cup at the edge of the table. It'll fall off.
examples.analysis: 边 is 'edge': 桌子边上 'at the edge of the table'. In speech 边 often takes 上 (边上). 放在 + place says where something is put, and 会…的 warns that it will happen.

examples.zh: 我坐边上就行，你们坐中间吧。
examples.en: I'm fine on the end. You guys take the middle.
examples.analysis: 边上 here is the side or end of a row of seats, set against 中间 'the middle'. …就行 'will do, is fine' shows you don't mind. 吧 makes the second half a friendly suggestion.

examples.en: Whose is that bag by the door?
examples.analysis: 门边 'by the door': 边 comes right after a thing to mean 'beside it'. 门边 describes 那个包 with no 的, and 是谁的? asks 'whose is it?'.

meaning: often, frequently, regularly

senses.en: often, frequently: something that happens again and again

examples.en: Do you come here to eat often?
examples.analysis: 经常 'often' goes before the verb phrase 来这儿吃饭. The two verbs follow in order: come here, then eat. 吗 turns the statement into a yes/no question.

examples.en: These days I often can't sleep well.
examples.analysis: 经常 + 睡不好 'often can't sleep well' describes a problem that keeps coming back, the kind of thing you tell a doctor. 最近 'lately' goes before 经常: time first, then how often.

examples.en: We don't see each other often.
examples.analysis: 不经常 'not often': 不 goes before 经常. 见面 'meet up' already means meeting each other, so no object follows it.

meaning: in a moment, shortly; (一会儿…一会儿…) one moment… the next…

senses.en: in a moment, a bit later (before the verb): 我一会儿就来
一会儿A，一会儿B: one moment A, the next B
a little while (after a verb): 等一会儿 'wait a moment'

examples.zh: 我一会儿就到，你们先吃吧。
examples.en: I'll be there in a minute. Go ahead and eat.
examples.analysis: Here 一会儿 comes before the verb and means 'in a moment, shortly'; 一会儿就… 'will … very soon' is a common pairing. Compare 等一会儿, where it follows the verb and means 'for a moment'.

examples.en: Are you free in a bit?
examples.analysis: 一会儿 is a time word here: 'a little later'. It goes before the verb phrase 有空儿 'have free time', the usual slot for time words. It is a light way to ask for a bit of someone's time soon.

examples.zh: 今天一会儿晴，一会儿下雨。
examples.en: Today it's sunny one minute and raining the next.
examples.analysis: 一会儿A，一会儿B means 'one moment A, the next B': two states keep switching. Both 一会儿 belong to the pattern, so both are marked. 晴 'sunny' is an adjective, so no verb is needed.

related.en: before long, soon after (about what happened)

meaning: word (a unit of vocabulary)

senses.en: word, term: 这个词 'this word'; a 词 may have one or more characters (字)

examples.en: What does this word mean?
examples.analysis: 词 is a word, which may be written with one character or more. 这个词 'this word' uses 个. …是什么意思? 'what does … mean?' is the standard way to ask.

examples.en: This word isn't used much anymore.
examples.analysis: 这个词 is the topic and 不常用了 comments on it: 常用 'commonly used', with 不 before it. 了 at the end marks a change: it used to be common, and now it isn't.

examples.en: I memorized twenty words today.
examples.analysis: 记 here is 'memorize'. Number + 个 + 词: 二十个词 'twenty words'. The 了 after 记 marks the job as done.

meaning: about the same; almost, nearly; good enough

senses.en: about the same, similar; good enough: 这两个差不多
almost, nearly, about: 差不多好了 'almost ready'

examples.en: I'm about as tall as he is.
examples.analysis: A 跟 B 差不多 + adjective 'A and B are about equally …': 差不多高 'about the same height'. Here 差不多 works like an adverb before the adjective 高.

examples.zh: 饭差不多好了，过来吃吧。
examples.en: The food's almost ready. Come and eat.
examples.analysis: 差不多 before 好了 means 'almost': the food is nearly done. 过来吃吧 'come over and eat' is the call to the table.

examples.zh: 这两个差不多，随便买一个吧。
examples.en: These two are pretty much the same. Just buy either one.
examples.analysis: Here 差不多 is the predicate, an adjective meaning 'about the same', with no 很 or 是. 随便买一个 'buy any one' follows because the difference does not matter.

collocations.en: more or less, I guess (a vague answer)

meaning: scary, frightening; awful, terrible

senses.en: scary, frightening: 这个电影很可怕
awful, terrible in a frightening or shocking way (storm, accident, bad news): 太可怕了; not for 'poor quality' (bad food is 难吃)

examples.en: Is this movie scary?
examples.analysis: 可怕 'scary' is the predicate of 这个电影, with no 是 before it. 可怕 describes the thing that causes fear, while 怕 'to be afraid' describes how a person feels.

examples.zh: 昨天晚上的雨太可怕了。
examples.en: Last night's rain was really frightening.
examples.analysis: 太可怕了 'so scary, awful' is a common reaction to storms, accidents or bad news. 昨天晚上的 describes 雨: 'last night's rain'.

examples.zh: 这只狗一点儿也不可怕。
examples.en: This dog isn't scary at all.
examples.analysis: 一点儿也不 + adjective 'not … at all' strengthens the denial: 一点儿也不可怕 'not scary in the slightest'. 只 is the measure word for the dog.

related.en: to be afraid of (the person feels it)
to feel awful (in body or mind): describes how you feel, unlike 可怕, which describes a thing

meaning: center (of a place); a center (a facility)

senses.en: the center of a place: 市中心 'city center, downtown'
a center as a facility: 体育中心 'sports center'

examples.zh: 我住在市中心，上班很方便。
examples.en: I live downtown, so getting to work is easy.
examples.analysis: 市中心 'city center': 市 'city' + 中心 'center', a place word after 住在. The second half gives the result; Chinese often needs no 'so' between the two halves.

examples.zh: 我们去体育中心打球吧。
examples.en: Let's go play ball at the sports center.
examples.analysis: 中心 here is a facility: 体育中心 'sports center'. The type comes first and 中心 last, as in English. 去 + place + activity says where you go and what for.

examples.en: Excuse me, which floor is the exam center on?
examples.analysis: 考试中心 'exam center' is the subject; 在几楼? asks which floor it is on. 几 asks for a number, and floors are numbered, so 几楼 means 'which floor'.

related.en: the middle between things or of a row (坐中间); not for a city center: 市中心, not 市中间
